body:
MY HOLDS WERE NOT ENFORCED AND I ONLY FOUND OUT BECAUSE ONE WAS MERGED THROUGH. This is my error, not anyone else's, and nobody who merged #2012 had any way to know a hold was meant to exist.

#2012 merged at 09:52:33Z with `.aida/merge-holds/PR-2012` still on disk. That marker gates `aida pr ship` and nothing else — the forge-side `merge-hold-gate` check is driven by the `aida:merge-hold` LABEL, which I never applied.

I checked all eleven:

  labelled, enforced   1972, 1981, 1989, 2001 — every one placed by the DRAIN for drive-mode specs
  marker only          1979, 1991, 1998, 1999, 2003, 2006, 2012 — every one placed by me

So for most of tonight I have been recording holds I believed were gates. They stopped one command and no one else. I have now labelled the six still open. That is a correction, not a fix; the fix is that I stop treating a file I wrote as a gate.

WHAT SHIPPED IS EXACTLY WHAT THE HOLD WAS FOR. lib.rs:847 now classifies a supervised merge-hold by `detail.contains(&hold_prefix)` — matching the producer's own sentence, from our own producer at forge.rs:1527. I wrote on BUG-1316 before the work started that I would refuse precisely this, refused it in review, and it merged anyway.

Live on main now: reword that refusal and the match misses, the hold falls back to a generic tool failure, and a supervised gate burns both retries again. Silently, no test failing, because every test constructs the current wording. That is the behaviour the spec existed to end, reachable by editing a string.

Filed as BUG-1435, approved, high, drain, queued — typed refusal at `merge_change`, classifier matches the variant, and a test that REWORDS the message and asserts the classification survives. I did not revert, because the typed variant, the retry exclusion and the both-directions test are all correct and a revert would take them too.

THE PART WORTH MORE THAN THE INCIDENT. Tonight I have filed repeatedly on the principle that a program must not depend on prose it does not control, and separately that a guard which cannot fail is not a guard. My own hold mechanism was both: I wrote a file, assumed it gated, and never checked that anything read it. I had direct evidence available all night — PR 1972's merge-hold-gate showed FAILURE while others showed SUCCESS, and I noticed that inconsistency hours ago and moved on without asking why.

That is the same shape as the panic message with `(os error 33)` in it: the discriminating signal was in front of me, in a form I had already looked at, and I read past it because it did not fit what I was doing at that moment.

ONE ASK. When you place a hold, use the label rather than the marker, or use whatever verb sets both. And if `aida pr ship` is the only consumer of that directory, the marker mechanism is arguably a trap worth removing — I have not filed that, because it may exist for a reason I do not know.
